ShortDescription.Value: Progressive job seeking for small cities

Publish.LongDescription:
Supported/recommended mods: Progression Control and Hard Mode Continued. Unsupported mods: Code mods that override the same game systems are generally incompatible. Check the Override folder on GitHub for the systems overridden by this mod.
I added option to enable full physical simulation, its false by default, but I highly recommend it until no performance issues (should be set before loading game) . In the vanilla game, workers already have a 59% chance of having a day off even in small cities, which is very unrealistic, and this chance increases further as the city grows. I added a progressive option that starts at 20% in small cities and gradually returns to vanilla behavior as the population passes the configured milestones. ## Small City Jobs
**Small City Jobs** is designed to make employment behave more naturally in small towns and villages.
In the vanilla game, citizens can be surprisingly reluctant to take available jobs when only a small number of suitable positions exist. This works reasonably well in large cities with hundreds of vacancies, but can cause unrealistic behaviour in small settlements, where even a handful of open jobs may represent a significant part of the local economy.
The goal of this mod is not to replace the vanilla employment system, but to make it scale better with city size.
In smaller cities, citizens are more willing to take available jobs, accept reasonable alternatives, and look for better employment opportunities. The mod also reduces situations where adults leave employment or choose studying simply because the local job market is small, including cases where they would otherwise travel outside the city to study despite suitable work being available.
As the population grows, these adjustments gradually fade and the game returns toward its original behaviour.
The mod also adds **UI and life-path improvements** intended to make employment-related behaviour easier to understand. Their purpose is to expose more of what citizens are doing and why, making it easier to follow individual citizens and understand the effects of the employment simulation.
The overall aim is to make villages and small towns function more naturally without making employment artificially easy in larger cities.
The transition can be configured in the game options, allowing the player to decide how quickly vanilla behaviour should be restored.
**Detailed mechanics, settings and individual changes are documented in the forum discussion.**
Please report bugs and leave feedback in the discussion section/forum. Updated screenshots.
Publish.ChangeLog: Full Traffic – Adds an option to disable the game's traffic reduction, allowing full citizen traffic to be simulated. Milestone-Based Days Off – Reduces days off in small cities and gradually returns them toward the vanilla behavior as the population passes the configured milestones.
